_note: Rule file for eval/redact_agent_session.py.
The real one -- eval/redaction_rules.local.json -- is deliberately NOT committed,
and this example ships in its place. The reason is the whole point of the tool: a
rule's anchor is a verbatim copy of the sentence it removes, so a committed rule
file would republish, in one convenient list, exactly the content the redaction
took out of the transcripts. The first version of this project did commit the
anchors inline in the Python source, and a secret scan across the files going
public is what caught it.
What ships instead is this structure plus the category-by-category counts in
logs/agent_sessions/README.md, which is what a reader actually needs: how much was
removed, of what kind, and the assurance that nothing technical was among it.
Anchors below are placeholders. Substitute real ones to use this file.
Fields:
redactions[].start     literal text to remove (exact, not a pattern)
redactions[].end       remove start..end inclusive; null removes only start
redactions[].category  shown in the marker left behind, so keep it truthful
regex[].pattern        for content that appears in more than one wording --
compaction summaries paraphrase earlier messages, so an
exact anchor matches the original and misses the restatement
probes[]               strings that must not survive anywhere in the output, no
matter which rule was supposed to catch them. Independent of
the rules on purpose: 'is each rule's own anchor gone' is a
circular check and passed every leak this tool ever had
Probe the MIDDLE of a sentence, not its opening. This is the one that got past a
passing run and into a pushed commit: every probe was the first few words of a
removed sentence, a compaction summary had quoted one from the middle, and so every
rule matched, every probe passed, and four fragments shipped anyway. A probe list is
only as wide as the phrasings it thought to look for. Include interior phrases, and
when a leak is found, add the phrase that was missed rather than only the rule.
Order matters. A span rule (end set) must come before a bare-anchor rule on the same
start string, or the bare rule consumes the opening anchor and the span never fires.

redactions.category: pasted third-party evaluation, not an instruction
pasted third-party evaluation, not an instruction

probes: <a distinctive word from the removed content>
